correctness.rationale: The graph and the complete clique complex use the same six differences as the quotient of the triangular tessellation by L={(a,b):a+3b=0 mod 13}. The quotient has the stated face vector and is a torus. Independent enumeration modulo the span of triangle boundaries reproduced boundary rank 25, 78 unoriented simple four-cycles, the homology census 39+13+13+13, two affine orbits of size 39, and one translation orbit of size 13 for each nonzero class. Every three-cycle is filled, so the nonzero four-cycles establish minimality (an even edge cycle decomposes into simple cycles). As another check, the triangular step norm yields exactly the three signed pairs of nonzero displacements at length four, with representatives (3,−1), (1,4), and their sum (4,3). They reduce to the three distinct nonzero classes of L/2L. evidence: H1 is the exhibited rank-two lattice; the three directions form a basis and its sum up to sign. The earlier proof gives a translation orbit of 13 per integral direction, affine transitivity on the essential shell, and an equivariant central-edge identification for the null rhombi.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: H1 with mod-two coefficients is L/2L (H0 is torsion-free). All named four-cycle carriers reduce as asserted, and absence of shorter essential integral cycles implies absence of shorter mod-two ones. The affine group is transitive on graph edges because its multipliers act transitively on Q and translations on vertices; hence it is transitive on the 39 edge-associated rhombi. This recovers both affine orbits and all three translation orbits without a new census.
